clinician.trajectory_summary: A 55-year-old woman presented with palpitations and dysphagia. Chest radiographs revealed a smooth, round mass >7 cm in the middle mediastinum between the trachea and vertebral bodies. CT imaging demonstrated a lobulated tumor (75 × 57 × 80 mm) in the upper to middle mediastinum with homogenous inner component, compressing the esophagus. MRI confirmed no invasion of surrounding organs. Upper endoscopy showed a smooth elevated lesion with venous dilation at 22 cm from the incisor teeth, consistent with external esophageal compression. Surgical resection was performed, revealing a mass ~8 cm adjacent to the mid-thoracic esophagus; subtotal esophagectomy and esophagogastrostomy were performed due to extensive defect in the esophageal adventitia and muscular layer. Histopathological examination of the resected specimen revealed spindle-shaped cells in fasciculated and disarrayed architecture with nuclei in a palisading pattern—morphology characteristic of schwannoma. Postoperative course was uneventful with no evidence of recurrence.
